title: Quality Control
description:
Studied statistical quality control methods used to evaluate process performance, analyze variation, and support quality improvement decisions.

Key Topics Covered:

Confidence Intervals: Point and interval estimation, confidence intervals for population means, proportions, variance, and standard deviation, and sample size determination.

Hypothesis Testing: Null and alternative hypotheses, significance levels, P-values, Z-tests, statistical decision-making, and sample size considerations.

Quality Improvement: Structured problem-solving, root cause identification, corrective actions, and the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle.

Statistical Process Control: Process stability, control limits, and the distinction between common-cause and assignable-cause variation.

Process Capability: Evaluation of process performance against specification limits using Cp, Cpk, Pp, and Ppk indices.

Knowledge Gained:

Developed an understanding of how statistical analysis and quality improvement methods support process monitoring, variation reduction, and data-driven decisions in manufacturing environments.
skills: Process Capability Analysis (Cp, Cpk, Pp, Ppk)
